data.gender_notes: Body is used as a unisex name in christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The meaning of Body is recorded in name-lists as “Temple of the Holy Spirit”. This meaning has NOT been verified against a classical lexical or onomastic source, so it is published as an unverified candidate only. The record is flagged for manual source verification.
data.spiritual_meaning: Body expresses “Temple of the Holy Spirit”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Body total 19, reducing to 1. Number 1 is associated with leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: בּוֹדֶיךָ
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The Hebrew word for body is derived from the word 'boded', which means 'your work'. In a biblical context, it can refer to the physical body as the work of God, or to the body as the vessel for the soul.

in_greek.name: σῶμα
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek word for body is 'soma'. It is used extensively in the New Testament to refer to the physical body, as well as to the body of Christ and the body of the church.

in_latin.name: corpus
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin word for body is 'corpus'. It is used in various religious and philosophical contexts, including in the Latin Vulgate Bible and in Catholic theology.

biblical_reference.verse_reference: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
biblical_reference.note: The Hebrew word 'nephesh' is used in this verse to refer to the living soul, which can be translated as body or self. The body is thus created as the vessel for the soul, and both are essential aspects of human existence.
